business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- AJC Jewel Manufacturers Ltd. (BSE: 544425) describes itself as a leading integrated B2B jewellery manufacturing and technology platform, complementing its established B2B gold jewellery manufacturing with a differentiated D2C retail platform for contemporary silver jewellery under Esthara Jewels.
- Deck cites favourable industry structural trends: India's gems and jewellery exports were USD 27.72 billion in FY2025-26, with silver jewellery exports growing 52.21% YoY to USD 1.47 billion, supporting AJC's push into organised silver jewellery retail.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: B2B Gold: 22K/18K casting & studded jewellery via digital portal; 2.5L+ designs; low MOQ; 15-day production cycle. D2C Silver (Esthara): 925 Sterling + 2.5-micron gold-plated; 50% gross margin; sold via owned stores & e-commerce; 5 stores under fit-out in Kerala for H1 FY27

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Onboarded Kalyan Jewellers and Chemmanur; serving 300+ independent jewellers; IIBX Jeweller onboarding in progress

guidance.title: Guidance / outlook
guidance.body: Targeting 50% CAGR over 3 years; FY27 standalone revenue guidance of ~₹450 Cr; Sharjah acquisition expected to add ~₹60 Cr by end FY27; 120% capacity expansion planned; Esthara silver retail to scale to 5+ stores in H1 FY27

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: International expansion via Sharjah hub (GCC access); pan-India rollout (North, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka); B2C e-commerce platform launch; CNC-machined jewellery as high-margin new category; potential export growth via UAE free zone

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: B2B EBITDA margin: 4.81% (FY26); PAT margin: 2.69% (FY26); Esthara silver D2C margin: ~50%; cost reduction via CNC & automation; bullion sourcing efficiency via Sharjah

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: IPO proceeds funding capex (CNC, Sharjah, Esthara retail); debt reduction priority; no dividend history disclosed; reinvestment in design R&D and manufacturing scale

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Geopolitical delays in Sharjah acquisition; reliance on few large corporate clients (Kalyan, Chemmanur); silver retail execution risk in D2C; raw material price volatility; regulatory changes in hallmarking/GST compliance

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Esthara’s 50% D2C silver margin is unusually high for jewellery retail — enabled by vertical integration (manufacturing + direct sales), bypassing wholesale markups entirely, creating a hidden profit engine.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body: - [Guidance] Management reiterated prior guidance of targeting a consolidated revenue CAGR of approximately 50% over the next three years, with standalone revenue of around ₹450 crore in FY27, with the Esthara Jewels retail expansion expected to contribute to this.
